test_path: (no dedicated test — exercised via app routing tests)

findings.failing_input: `const store = params.get('store') ?? defaults.filters.store;` — store is taken AS-IS from URL params. An attacker (or a stale bookmark) could put any string into ?store= and it would render into the dashboard's Filters.store, potentially as a label or trigger a query against a non-existent store. Then downstream code may not validate strictly.
findings.expected: Validate that store is in a known list (read from store-meta) before accepting.
findings.fix_sketch: Pass valid store names to readDashboardState; reject unknown.

findings.failing_input: DATE_RX is shape-only; not calendar-validated. ?from=2026-99-99&to=2026-99-99&preset=custom would parse successfully and pass through to API routes which would then 400 via the parseRangeParams isRealDate check. UX: user sees blank tab.
findings.fix_sketch: Use isRealDate (or import isDate from dateValidation) before accepting.
findings.regression_test_idea: readDashboardState with ?preset=custom&from=2026-99-99 → falls back to defaults.filters.range.

uncertainty_notes: Symmetric read/write functions; URL stays clean by omitting defaults; replaceState avoids history pollution. Two minor input-validation gaps (STA-21 store, STA-22 dates) are MINOR because downstream API routes have their own validation that 400s on bad input — UX degraded but no data corruption.
